I am 63 years old, and I have worked this land for 40 years. There are only two of us at home now, so I must plan with my own two hands in mind. My farm is 16.1 mu, and I know every corner of it.

My wheat is already in the field from last autumn. I have 10 mu of it. It is coming up green, and I will top-dress it with urea when the weather settles. I will irrigate three times: the green-up water, the jointing water, and one more when the grain is filling. I use improved wheat seeds—varieties from the local seed station I have trusted for years. I will spray twice: once for weeds and once if I see aphids or rust. The ground was rotary-tilled before I sowed it last year.

I keep 6.1 mu of cotton. Cotton earns more money than grain, but it is backbreaking work with all the spraying and hand-picking. At my age, I will not plant more than I can manage between the two of us. I will rotary-till the cotton field, sow hybrid cotton seed, and put down fertilizer. Cotton is thirsty and the bollworms never sleep, so I will irrigate three times and spray five times through the season. If the weather is fair, I expect about 250 kg of seed cotton per mu.

When the wheat is harvested in early June, I will put summer maize on those same 10 mu. Time is short, so I will use no-tillage direct seeding right into the wheat stubble—saves my back, saves time, and keeps the moisture. Hybrid maize seed is the only choice if you want a crop. Two irrigations and two sprays will see it through. I expect about 520 kg per mu.

I have my well, so water is there, but the pump costs electricity. I do not waste a drop. After 40 years, I know that being stingy with fertilizer or pesticide only robs your own table.
